HowItWorks.title: How it works
HowItWorks.metaDescription: Kvaterka connects tenants and hosts directly: you pay each other for the rental, and the platform takes 5% from the host after the rental is completed.
HowItWorks.lede: Kvaterka isn't a classifieds board. It's a platform that remembers what happened: who agreed with whom, whether the rental actually took place, and what both sides said about each other afterward.

search.title: Find an apartment
search.body: Search understands not just "daily" and "yearly" but everything in between — from a few days to several months.

request.title: Send a request
request.body: This isn't a booking yet: the host sees your request and responds. If they don't respond in time, the request expires on its own, and you're not left wondering.

negotiate.title: Work out the details in messages
negotiate.body: Before confirmation, messaging stays inside the platform. That way both sides keep a record of what was agreed, in case a dispute comes up later.

checkin.title: Check in and mark your arrival
checkin.body: The exact address opens up after confirmation — until then, only the neighborhood shows on the map.

confirm.title: Confirm the rental happened
confirm.body: Both sides do this. It's the confirmation, not the payment, that closes out the rental.

review.title: Leave a review
review.body: Both sides' reviews publish at the same time, so nobody can read the other one first and shape theirs to match.

host.heading: For hosts
host.p1: Posting is free. Your listing goes through moderation, then appears in search. You respond to requests, confirm the rental, and get paid directly by the tenant.
host.p2Rich: The platform takes a 5% fee — only from the host, and only after both sides confirm the rental happened. More about the fee.

money.heading: The platform doesn't touch rental money
money.body: You hand over the rent and deposit to each other directly, as agreed. Kvaterka isn't a party to your deal, doesn't accept rental payments, and doesn't hold your money.
money.noteRich: What this means in practice. The platform can't "give you your money back", because it never received it. What it can do is keep the message history, the check-in and check-out confirmations, and review a dispute based on those records.
